edges.description: Without SPACR, a main chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan of the IPM, the matrix around rod and cone outer segments is not assembled normally.
The matrix holds outer segments in alignment; when it is disorganized the outer segments lose their alignment and are shortened.

The authors of the knockout study propose that the disorganized matrix impairs the RPE, possibly by weakening outer-segment recognition and attachment before phagocytosis. This step is a stated hypothesis.
Proposed in the knockout study: impaired handling of shed outer segments leaves degraded material in the subretinal space.
The knockout study links the dysfunctional photoreceptors to the regions next to the accumulated material and disorganized matrix.
Autofluorescent hyperreflective deposits form between outer segments and RPE.
edges.limitations: Mice have no macula, so the deposits are scattered across the fundus rather than forming a single central vitelliform lesion; a single yolk-like dome was seen in one mouse only.

edges.description: Late-onset, slowly progressive loss of rod and cone function and outer retinal thinning.
edges.limitations: Degeneration is mild and late (detectable from 9 months), and the mouse shows no pigment deposits, so the retinitis pigmentosa fundus picture is not reproduced.

nodes.description: In 14-month-old Impg1 knockout mice the RPE apical microvilli are sparse, Bruch's membrane is abnormal, and lipid droplets accumulate in RPE cells next to subretinal debris. The knockout study proposes that a defective matrix impairs recognition and phagocytosis of shed outer segments, overloading the RPE with undigested material.

nodes.description: Both IMPG1 alleles carry a null variant (nonsense, canonical splice-site, exon-skipping splice variant) or a hypomorphic missense variant, so the photoreceptors secrete little or no functional SPACR into the interphotoreceptor matrix. In the founding families at least one allele was a nonsense or presumed frameshift allele, and a leaky splice variant (c.807+5G>A) skips exon 7 in about half of transcripts. Carriers of one null allele in recessive families are clinically unaffected or only subclinically affected, which is the basis for separating this entity from the dominant IMPG1 disease, where a heterozygous missense allele such as p.Leu238Arg is proposed to act dominantly within the matrix.

nodes.description: SPACR is made by rod and cone photoreceptors and, with SPACRCAN (IMPG2), supplies most of the chondroitin sulfate of the interphotoreceptor matrix and the cone-specific glycocalyx. Loss of SPACR removes chondroitin sulfate and cone-associated PNA lectin staining from the outer-segment compartment of the matrix, and in older knockout mice the matrix becomes vacuolated and disorganized.

nodes.description: Autofluorescent, hyperreflective material accumulates between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE. In patients this forms the central vitelliform lesion, sometimes with multifocal deposits; in knockout mice, which lack a macula, the deposits appear across the whole fundus from about 9 months and grow with age. In IMPG1 disease the material sits above the RPE, unlike BEST1 disease, where it lies between the RPE and Bruch's membrane.
